messages:
incident_bot: [PAGER] Sev 2 alert for OpalCorp (private VPC) — multiple egress failures detected, NLB health checks failing across primary region, customers seeing 502/timeout. INC-2151239999 :rotating_light: https://incidents.internal/INC-2151239999

sophie_netops: I'm on it. I'm seeing a big spike of SecurityGroupRevoke events from cleanup-lambda around 03:11:34 UTC. NLB health checks (from our health-subnet 10.4.3.0/24) are being rejected by the tenant SGs.

raj_oncall: paging netops + platform. @leo_platform can you confirm target group health for opalcorp-primary? any recent deploys/changes?

leo_platform: no deploys in the last 2h from platform side. Checking target-group now — health shows 1/3 -> 2/3 but failing checks still present. Getting the instance logs.

maria_se: customer impact from support: OpalCorp's dashboard (internal tenant) intermittent 502s since ~03:10 UTC; ~12-15% request fail rate reported. They're using our private NLB + SG restricted to their app subnets.

sophie_netops: looks like the cleanup-lambda mistakenly removed a CIDR allowlist entry used for NLB health checks. event sample: 
```
CloudTrail: RevokeSecurityGroupIngress sg-0abc1234 revoked 10.4.3.0/24 tcp:443 by lambda:cleanup-sg
```
This matches the timing.

leo_platform: if we re-add the SG rule quickly health checks should recover. I can apply a temporary allow and then we can rollback the lambda.

raj_oncall: plan: 1) temp allow health-subnet to tenant SG 2) disable cleanup lambda 3) shift small DNS weight to standby region if health not recover within 2m 4) postmortem + rollback checklist. Anyone opposed?

sophie_netops: doing step 1 now. Command I'm running: 
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc1234 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.4.3.0/24 --description "INC-2151239999 temp allow healthchecks"
```

leo_platform: received. Applying.

devops-bot: action_log: security-group-update sg-0abc1234 +10.4.3.0/24 (author: sophie_netops)

leo_platform: NLB target health improving — 2/3 -> 3/3 for primary TG within 45s. Starting traffic verification.

maria_se: heads up — Ops team, email to OpalCorp sent (brief): we detected network policy churn that affected ingress to your NLB; mitigation in progress. No data loss expected.

dns_ops: prepped standby region record. If we need to shift: change-set ready for weighted record 
```
{ "ChangeBatch": { "Changes": [ { "Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": { "Name": "api.opalcorp.private", "Type": "A", "SetIdentifier": "standby-eu", "Weight": 80, "TTL": 60, "ResourceRecords": [ {"Value":"10.200.2.45"} ] } } ] } }
```

raj_oncall: good. @dns_ops keep on standby but hold — health is trending green.

leo_platform: confirmed application-level checks passing and synthetic traffic to opalcorp shows 200s. Rolling back the immediate mitigation in a minute but keeping the SG rule annotated for audit.

sophie_netops: disabling cleanup-lambda (cleanup-sg) now to prevent recurrence. Command: 
```
aws lambda update-function-configuration --function-name cleanup-sg --environment "Variables={ENABLED=false}"
```

devops-bot: lambda-update cleanup-sg -> ENV ENABLED=false (author: sophie_netops)

leo_platform: capture: tcpdump run on one of the targets for 60s, attaching pcap to the ticket. No suspicious traffic patterns beyond healthcheck rejects.

maria_se: I've informed OpalCorp that traffic is restored and we're keeping watch for 30m. They asked for root cause and ETA for postmortem.

raj_oncall: incident status: mitigation applied, customer impact reduced to near 0, monitoring for recurrence. Downgrading severity to P2. Assigning postmortem owner: sophie_netops.

sophie_netops: will own postmortem. Immediate action items: 1) restore SG rules snapshot to managed state 2) add guardrail to cleanup-lambda to ignore tenant SGs with tag tenant:critical 3) create runbook step to pause lambda on detected health-check rejects 4) notify security for review.

incident_bot: INC-2151239999 update — status: mitigated, severity -> P2, runbook_created: true, assignee: sophie_netops.

dns_ops: leaving DNS change queued but not applied. If any sign of recurrence we'll enact weighted failover.

leo_platform: I recommend we add a scheduled regression test to trigger after cleanup-lambda runs in staging to catch this pattern.

maria_se: Customer confirmation: OpalCorp acknowledges recovery and appreciates quick response. They'll wait for root cause and timeline for full fix.

raj_oncall: closing rotation — thanks everyone. Keep the pcap and CloudTrail events attached to INC ticket. Postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sophie_netops: attaching pcap and ct-logs to INC-2151239999 now. Will kick off postmortem doc and link here.

incident_bot: thread archived for INC-2151239999. If any new events reopen the incident channel.
